copy.title: The Jordan Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of Michael Jordan’s family: who owns what, which stocks you can buy, the homes, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #024 · The Jordan family · Data as of
copy.h1: Air Jordan has a family. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, what each of them owns, which of their companies you can buy stock in, the homes, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file: what they own, what’s on the record, and where every fact comes from. Michael’s kids are listed by first name only.
copy.investLede: You can buy shares of DraftKings, where Michael became an investor in 2020, and of Nike, which pays him but isn’t his. The rest are private.
copy.moneyLede: His NBA salaries added up to about $90 million. Most of his fortune came later, from Nike and the Hornets. He’s the only one here with a published net worth.
copy.homesTitle: Listed at $29 million, sold for $9.5 million
copy.homesLede: His Chicago-area estate took 12 years to sell. For that house, the first number is what SI says he spent in all, including building it. Other prices are as reported. No street addresses here.
copy.homesChart: Each home: what it cost him, and what it sold for
copy.recordLede: The money in the team deals, the NASCAR case and the divorce. Records and reporting, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From a Nike deal in 1984 to a $4.7 billion fortune in 2026.

summary.t: Won six NBA titles with the Chicago Bulls. Forbes says his playing salaries totaled about $90 million, while deals with Nike, Hanes and Gatorade have paid him ten figures.

owns.t: Bought control of the team, then the Bobcats, for $275 million in 2010. Sold the majority in 2023 at a valuation of about $3 billion. Forbes says he reportedly kept a minority stake.
His 1984 Nike deal paid $500,000 a year plus royalties. Forbes says Nike now pays him nearly $300 million a year.
Joined the sports-betting company as a special adviser to its board and an investor in September 2020.
Co-owns the NASCAR team with Denny Hamlin. Forbes dates his NASCAR ownership to 2020.
Co-founded the tequila brand with four partners. It launched in 2019.

record.t: Bought control of the Charlotte Bobcats for $275 million in 2010. Sold minority stakes to Gabe Plotkin in 2019 and to Plotkin and Daniel Sundheim in 2020, then sold the majority to a group led by Plotkin and Rick Schnall in 2023, at a valuation of about $3 billion. NBA owners approved it 29–1.

His 23XI Racing team and Front Row Motorsports filed a federal antitrust suit against NASCAR after refusing its September 2024 charter offers. NASCAR settled on Dec. 11, 2025, the trial’s ninth day, and agreed to make charters permanent for its teams. No financial terms were reported.
Juanita Vanoy’s 2006 settlement was reported at $168 million, among the largest at the time.

facts.t: He was the NBA’s highest-paid player in only two of his 15 seasons.
Cincoro’s bottle tilts at 23 degrees, for his jersey number. He worked on the design with Nike’s Mark Smith.
In 2015 he cut the Highland Park asking price to $14.855 million. The digits add up to 23.
Forbes gives his residence as Jupiter, Florida.

kidsNote.t: Five children: Jeffrey, Marcus and Jasmine with Juanita Vanoy, and Victoria and Ysabel with Yvette Prieto. Names only; no photos of the kids.

summary.t: A loan officer from Chicago’s South Side when she met Michael in 1985. They married in Las Vegas in November 1989, and the divorce was final in December 2006.

record.t: Reported at $168 million, citing Crain’s Chicago Business, one of the largest in sports history at the time.

facts.t: She first filed for divorce in 2002, then withdrew the petition a month later.

summary.t: Cuban-born model. She met Michael at a Miami nightclub in 2008, and they married in April 2013.

facts.t: Besides modeling, she has worked for her parents’ company, at a hospital and in real estate.

summary.t: Served in the U.S. Air Force, then worked as an aircraft mechanic and equipment supervisor. He married Deloris Peoples in 1958. He was killed at a highway rest area in Lumberton, North Carolina, on July 23, 1993; two men were convicted of his murder.

facts.t: In 1996 Michael founded a Chicago-area Boys & Girls Club and dedicated it to him.

summary.t: A former bank employee and mother of five. She co-wrote children’s books about Michael, including Salt in His Shoes and Michael’s Golden Rules.

record.t: Her publisher’s bio names her work with the James R. Jordan Foundation in Chicago and the Jordan Institute for Families at UNC-Chapel Hill.

facts.t: Also wrote the parenting book Family First: Winning the Parenting Game.

summary.t: Michael’s younger sister. With their mother, she co-wrote the children’s books Salt in His Shoes and Did I Tell You I Love You Today?

companies.name: Charlotte Hornets
companies.who: Michael (controlling owner 2010–23; minority stake reported since)
companies.t: NBA team. Michael bought control for $275 million in 2010 and sold the majority in 2023 at a valuation of about $3 billion. No public shares.

companies.name: Nike (Jordan Brand)
companies.who: Michael (royalty deal since 1984; no reported stake)
companies.t: Jordan Brand is part of Nike, a public company. Forbes says Nike pays Michael nearly $300 million a year, but he has no reported ownership stake.

companies.name: DraftKings
companies.t: Sports-betting company. Michael joined as a special adviser to its board and an investor in September 2020. Forbes doesn’t give the size of his stake.

companies.name: 23XI Racing
companies.t: NASCAR Cup Series team. It sued NASCAR with Front Row Motorsports; NASCAR settled in December 2025 and made team charters permanent.

companies.name: Cincoro Tequila
companies.t: Launched in 2019 by Michael, Wyc Grousbeck, Emilia Fazzalari, Jeanie Buss and Wes Edens. Bottles cost $70 to $1,600 at launch. Derek Jeter and Serena Williams joined the founders as partners in 2024.

props.name: Highland Park estate
props.note: He bought the land in 1991 and built the house. SI says it cost him about $50 million in all, with renovations. First listed at $29 million in 2012.

summary.note: What the Highland Park, Ill., estate sold for in December 2024, after 12 years on the market. It was first listed at $29 million in 2012.

extra.t: He cut the asking price to $14.855 million in 2015 and kept it there for nine years. The digits add up to 23, his jersey number.
SI also lists a mansion in Utah, a penthouse in Chicago and two more homes in North Carolina. Forbes gives his residence as Jupiter, Florida.
